analyst_view.overall: A relegation six-pointer: Mainz (13th, 10 points) have lost five competitive games in a row, the latest 3-1 at Augsburg, and Urs Fischer admits the team is unsettled; Union (17th, 7 points) are five league games without a win after a 5-1 home defeat to Leipzig. Union are without centre-back Zeno Van den Bosch (fifth yellow card, already counted by the numbers) plus long-term absentees Markgraf and Nsoki, with Burcu and Trimmel doubtful; one site still lists Felix Uduokhai as banned, but his two-match ban from October should be served, so I don't count it. Mainz report no injuries beyond goalkeeper Schwolow missing training. It is Fischer's first meeting with his old club; no referee is named yet. I only expect a tenser, more physical game than the numbers do.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already add for Van den Bosch's ban (about +6% to Mainz) and the head-to-head. Union have scored only 4 in six and both teams are low on confidence, which argues for a cagey game, but Mainz have conceded 16 in six and Union just let in five. The two pull against each other, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Mainz expected to have more (5.9) at home, and they already count Union's low recent corner count. Nothing in the news changes how either side plays wide, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and already add a little for both sides' recent bookings (Union 17 in six). They don't count the stakes: 13th against 17th with both sides on losing runs is a nervy, physical fight, so I add 4%, to about 4.8; no referee is named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots and already add about 12% to Mainz for how many shots Union have been conceding. With Union's central defence thinned out that holds, and nothing else is new, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Mainz have been conceding plenty on target and Union create little, both of which the numbers already see, so I stay at 9.0.
